observations: What I read: the request JSON. With Read I viewed workflow/review/page-08.png and assets/panels/08-1.png, 08-2.png, 08-3.png and 08-4.png, and for the boundary review/page-07.png with the 07 assets. I compared these with storyboards/page-08.svg, the script in the request and source/original.txt lines 52-56. All files were readable. The runtime gave me no task ID, so task is null.
Text: all captions and labels match the source and script verbatim.

08-1: the caption covers the asset's blank top-left area and the window sky. Ravi's face, the hand at his chin and the phone in his lap are clear. Art note: a sliver of the asset's white unpainted block shows to the right of the caption (about x 299-327, y 24-166). It reads as blank sky at the window and does not affect reading.

08-2: the WELBUK VISION tag sits in the sky at top left. First reader's coverage note: the bottom caption (top edge y about 322) covers the specialist's lower torso and the base of the clinic. His face, his gesturing hand (protected [672,262,74,54], which ends at y 316) and the stethoscope are clear. Acceptable.

08-3: the tag and caption sit over the sky and the sofa arm at left. Ravi's pointing hand (around x 490-570) and the tablet (protected [583,681,159,103]) are clear of the caption, which ends at x 407. Faces are clear.

08-4, first reader's notes: the product label (x 704-985) starts about 5 px right of Ravi's face box (ends at 699). It sits beside his head and raised waving hand without covering either; it overlaps only part of his far shoulder and the background. The bottom caption covers Meera's lower legs and feet and reaches the edge of Ananya's feet. Neither is a face, hand or prop, and the phone in Meera's hand (at her right side) stays visible. Acceptable.

08-4 reading order (label at top right, tagline at bottom left): the label is read first, then the eye drops to the final tagline. A diagonal move to the last, closing line is normal and does not cause misreading.

First reader's 'us', the unintroduced vision characters and the repeated WELBUK VISION: these are verbatim or source-required (source line 4 requires marking future features as vision; lines 54-55 call the scenes symbolic). The vignette art and the tag keep both vision panels separate from the present. Acceptable.

Composite order: 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.'; WELBUK VISION, then 'The vision: trusted connections...'; WELBUK VISION, then 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.'; 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health', then 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.'.
There are no balloons on this page, so there are no tails to check. Teal tags and white narrator boxes are clearly different in style.

transitions.observation: From Ravi waving at the clinic door to Ravi on a train. The conditional caption marks a possible tomorrow, and his costume, bag and phone carry over.
Ravi's thoughtful look out of the window leads to the vignetted, tagged vision of a specialist at a clinic in another city, with dotted links between clinics.
The same vignette style and tag widen the vision to Ravi's family sharing a wellness tablet.
The vignette ends and the full-colour present-day clinic entrance returns, with the three main characters, the three product names and the closing tagline.

readingReview.comparison: My order matches the first reader's and the script. Their coverage notes are confirmed but cover no face, hand or protected prop. The narrative notes are source-faithful. Page 08 changed only as a neighbour, and its lettering passes.
